newsitem.title: JAPAN: Strong quake shakes area south of Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Strong quake shakes area south of Tokyo.

text.p: A strong earthquake shook a Japanese resort area south of Tokyo on Monday, causing some damage but no immediate reports of injuries, officials said.
The quake, at 11:09 p.m. (1409 GMT), measured five on the Japanese scale of seven in the city of Ito on the Izu Peninsula, strong enough to cause heavy damage to houses in populated areas.
"I was at home when the earthquake struck, but no objects fell off the shelves. But the house was shaking sideways for several minutes," said a spokesman for the Ito Fire Department.
"But I thought that if it continued longer, it could be serious," he said.
Police said a landslide triggered by the quake destroyed a house and there were water main breaks in the area of Ito, with a population of 72,000.
The quake was the latest in a series of tremors that have hit the earthquake-prone Izu Peninsula, 135 km (90 miles) south of Tokyo, known for its hot springs resorts.
The epicentre was on the east coast of the Izu Peninsula, about 10 kilometres (6.25 miles) under sea level, Japan's Meteorological Agency said.
The quake was the latest in a series of tremors that shook the area through the day.
Officials said nearly 1,200 minor tremors struck during the day, the strongest measuring 4.2 on the Richter scale.
Last October, the same region experienced a series of more than 5,000 tremors, only a few of which could be felt without seismic monitoring equipment, the agency said.
